newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Aircraft sees return to profitability.
newsitem.headline: Israel Aircraft sees return to profitability.

text.p: State-owned Israel Aircraft Industries (IAI) is likely to report a net profit this year for the first time in 10 years, an IAI spokesman said on Monday quoting president Moshe Keret.

The spokesman said Keret forecasted revenues of $1.6 billion from the company, compared with $1.45 billion in 1996. IAI sources said the company had a record orders backlog of $3 billion, compared with $2.5 billion the same time in 1996.
Keret attributed the turnaround to an improved world aviation market.

IAI has not published financial statements in recent years, but newspaper reports have said the company lost $40 million in 1996. The company laid off thousands of staff in the early 1990s as part of a recovery plan and reached a deal with banks to reschedule debts and provide new credit.

General Ismail Hakki Karadayi, the chief of the Turkish armed forces, is due to visit IAI headquarters on Wednesday to hold discussions on the Phantom fighter jet upgrade project IAI is carrying out for Turkey.
